static_traits.name: Li Ming
static_traits.family_status: Lives with parents and a younger sibling
static_traits.social_status: Relationship with teammates strained due to feeling of Being rejected; family support exists but feelings not yet fully shared
static_traits.medical_history: without similar psychological problem experiences;not yet received psychotherapy;No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Neutral attitude; willing to explore and reflect on own thoughts; able to clearly describe concrete situations; often using absolutist, negatively labeling expressions (like 'absolute failure')

basic_info.main_problem: 'I really like running fast, but I am not the fastest runner in the world, so overall I am an absolute failure (Being rejected).' This belief is affecting my self-esteem and overall confidence.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling to deal with these negative thoughts and improve my self-esteem, because they are affecting my athletic performance and overall well-being.
growth_experiences: Two years ago, after performing below Anticipation in a race, began comparing with other Athletes; initially moderate-intensity pressure, then gradually developed into: doubting one's ability and feeling like a failure whenever not winning first place; these feelings are mainly triggered in training and races, further affecting motivation, training enjoyment, and sleep.

core_beliefs: I am a complete failure (Being rejected)
Only being the best (fastest) counts as valuable

special_situations.event: Not yet winning first place in races or performing below Anticipation
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not the fastest, it means I am worthless and a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trains twice as hard, does positive self-talk, sets smaller goals to prove herself (but still uses 'must be first' as the standard)
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I failed again; I am an absolute failure

special_situations.event: Comparing with faster Athletes in training
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others run faster than me, it means I am not good enough and my value is lower
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Using comparison to motivate oneself but resulting in Reinforced self-blame and Self-denial, sometimes reducing contact with others
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them; I can never catch up

special_situations.event: When interacting with teammates, thinks about how they will view my results
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If teammates see me performing Average or not first, they will think I am useless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids in-depth communication with teammates, reducing sharing to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are all looking down on me

special_situations.event: At night before falling asleep, repeatedly recalling competition and training performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am still not fast enough now, I will keep performing badly in the future
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to gain a sense of control through constant thinking and Self-monitoring
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will fail in future races too; it is simply impossible to become the fastest

special_situations.event: There were a few occasions of arriving at events/competitions on time or early, but the overall impression is still of frequent lateness or mistakes
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If not doing one's best every time, occasional success does not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores positive evidence and focuses on negative exceptions to maintain high-standard self-demands
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: That time was just good luck; it does not show I have ability

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and accepted, and to prove self-worth through excellent performance
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged as not good enough or a failure, thus Being rejected and looked down upon
defense_goal: Protects self-esteem by maintaining extreme standards and self-labeling
Reducing sharing vulnerability with others to avoid the risk of being devalued

object_relations.self_representation: Self experienced as 'a Being rejected failure', an unreliable person
object_relations.object_representation: Others (teammates, parents, audience) are experienced as critical, judgmental observers

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites focusing on positive moments or examining labels such as 'absolute failure'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously worries that their objective failure will be downplayed, or that they will be judged like others do (transference: others = judge)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing in a gentle, rationalizing tone 'I may be naturally bad at time management/organization', sticking to the matter at hand, downplaying emotional expression, avoiding delving into shame and Fear.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to share real feelings with family or teammates and seek support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that sharing vulnerability will be seen as making excuses or being looked down on, bringing rejection and shame
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Describing only scheduling and time issues in a neutral, brief way, avoiding expressing the inner emotions of 'Being rejected', keeping a sense of distance.

manifestations: Highly bases self-worth on whether she is the 'fastest/first', with an either-or standard dominating the sense of meaning
Experiencing holistic failure and emptiness when performance does not meet standards
outcomes: Anxiety and Increased stress in training and races

manifestations: Reducing sharing and interaction out of fear of others' judgment
outcomes: Less support gained, negative cycle worsens

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Takes 'must be first / fastest' as the absolute standard of self-worth
Demanding of oneself with rule-based language like 'I should...'

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Believing teammates or other parents look down on and judge oneself
Before interactions, presets that others hold negative views of oneself

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Carefully avoids exposing vulnerability, reducing sharing of real feelings with others

exception_events.target_problem: In situations of taking children to sports activities, the client is usually highly tense and worried about being late, believing themselves unreliable, thus more prone to lateness and Self-denial.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Last month, arriving early at the race venue once, the client felt relief and pride, without the usual Self-denial and Anxiety intensified.
exception_events.reason: Clues: more relaxed at the time, not overthinking; the client also mentioned some 'luck' factors, indicating lighter pace and mental load, thus reducing lateness and negative cycles.

positive_force: Family relatively supportive; has potential support resources
The client is willing to explore and identify negative thought patterns (good cooperation)
Having arrived early and performed well before, positive evidence exists
Has tried positive self-talk and setting smaller goals
negative_force: Externalizes self-worth and ties it closely to 'first place / fastest'
Comparison and despair, mind reading and personalization causing Interpersonal tension
Ignoring positive evidence, Reinforcing failure experiences
Sleep impaired, decreased training enjoyment and drive

target_behavior.behavior: Strong Self-denial and Anxiety in training and races, accompanied by Decreased drive and avoiding active engagement
antecedent: Not yet winning first place in races or performing below Anticipation
Comparing with faster Athletes in training
When reviewing mistakes after the game
target_behavior.core_reason: The core belief 'if not the fastest, utterly worthless', deciding self-worth through external evaluation, forming black-and-white and comparison-type cognitive biases.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding feelings of failure and shame, trying to maintain control and motivation through self-criticism (maladaptive Reinforcement).
target_behavior.consequence: Grades and training quality decline, training enjoyment decreases, the negative cycle intensifies.

target_behavior.behavior: Developing Anxiety about being judged before and after interpersonal interactions (teammates, other parents) and Avoids communication
antecedent: When arriving late or perceiving a mistake
target_behavior.core_reason: Highly sensitive to others' evaluations, viewing others as judges, with mind reading and personalization cognitions appearing.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding possible criticism and rejection, reducing Anxiety in the short term.
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal tension, reduced access to support, Increased sense of loneliness.

target_behavior.behavior: Difficulty falling asleep (repeatedly thinking about negative performances and worrying about the future before sleep)
antecedent: In a stage of high focus on results before and after competitions
target_behavior.core_reason: Trying to gain certainty and control through repeated thinking, accompanied by catastrophizing/predicting-the-future worries.
target_behavior.function: Attempting to control emotions and outcomes through cognition (a maladaptive self-soothing strategy).
target_behavior.consequence: Declining sleep quality, next-day energy and performance impaired.
